newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Netanyahu moves against Palestinians in Jerusalem.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu moves against Palestinians in Jerusalem.

text.p: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu ordered police to shut four Palestinian offices in Jerusalem, flaunting Israel's hold on the city while Yasser Arafat paid a showcase visit to the United States.

The move, which Netanyahu said was directed against Palestinian self-rule activity in Jerusalem, drew PLO condemnation at a time of already high tensions over Israel's plan to build new Jewish homes in the eastern part of the city.
It also was likely to cloud a visit on Wednesday by the right-wing Israeli leader to Egypt, where he was due to hold talks with President Hosni Mubarak.
The Public Security Ministry, in charge of police, said warnings would be served on Wednesday on the four institutions in East Jerusalem, which it declined to name.
"If they do not close on their own accord within 48 hours, then warrants for their closure will be issued," a ministry spokeswoman said.

In a speech to U.S. Jewish leaders late on Tuesday, Netanyahu charged that several offices in East Jerusalem were operating illegally on behalf of the Palestinian Authority that is in charge of parts of the West Bank and Gaza Strip.
He gave no number but said it was "considerably less" than 20.
"We are going to shut down those offices...We are not asking Palestinians to shut them down. We are shutting them down," Netanyahu said.
Netanyahu also instructed Police Minister Avigdor Kahalani to "remove by the end of the week Palestinian security men operating in Jerusalem", the Israeli leader's spokesman said.
Under Israel-PLO peace deals, the Palestinian Authority cannot operate in East Jerusalem, whose final status is to be decided in future peace talks.
Faisal al-Husseini, the top PLO official in Jerusalem, said the threatened closures showed the Israeli government did not care about the peace process.
"Such arbitrary decisions will take the region back to the osphere of conflict between the Palestinians and the Israelis, which we had dreamed of ending," he told Voice of Palestine radio.

Netanyahu, under fire from Jewish settlers and other right-wingers over Israel's troop withdrawal from most of the West Bank town of Hebron in January, has repeatedly vowed to stand firm on Jerusalem.

Last year, the PLO closed two Palestinian offices in the east of the city after Israel demanded they be shut. The PLO said at the time it took the action to deprive Netanyahu of any excuse to slow peace efforts.

The new moves were announced only hours after Palestinian President Arafat said in Washington he still regarded Netanyahu as a peace partner despite plans to build 6,500 Jewish homes at Jabal Abu Ghneim, called Har Homa by Israel.
Netanyahu has said bulldozers will begin to move in two weeks on the pine-covered Jerusalem hill at the centre of an international controversy.
U.S. President Bill Clinton sided with Arafat at a White House meeting on Monday, saying Netanyahu's plan to build the homes in East Jerusalem would fuel "mistrust".
Israel captured East Jerusalem in the 1967 Middle East war and annexed it, a move not recognised internationally, to claim all the city as its capital.
The PLO sees construction at Jabal Abu Ghneim as an attempt to block its demand for East Jerusalem to become capital of a Palestinian state.
